clue.text: Hope for the right man: a divorced criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A party's hope is pinned on a man whose divorce has led him into crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges the letters of MAN, A and DIVORCED. 'Hope for the right' means the Conservative leader who was once the right wing's hope.
explanation.definitionFit: He led the Conservatives, the party of the political right, and was its great electoral hope.

clue.text: Prepared comeback-flash in pan maybe — then was quick to fold

parts.note: a flash of gold in a prospector's pan; AU is the chemical symbol for gold
tore means rushed, went quickly
a ply is a fold or layer

explanation.surface: Someone stung by a feeble retort that flashed and fizzled then hurriedly gave up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flash in pan' suggests the idiom for a short-lived success, but here it is a glint of gold in a prospector's pan.
explanation.definitionFit: An automatic email response is a reply written in advance, ready to be sent back.

clue.text: Most suspect poem on Jubilee inadequate

parts.note: If is Kipling's famous poem

indicators.note: inadequate means falling short, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: a jubilee is a celebration, a fiesta

explanation.surface: A verse for a royal jubilee is judged poor and highly dubious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inadequate' cuts the final A off FIESTA, leaving FIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is informal for doubtful or dodgy; the superlative is the most doubtful.

clue.text: This is to give credit, certainly!

definitions.text: This is to give credit, certainly!

parts.note: CR is the standard abbreviation for credit in accounts
yup is a casual way of saying yes, certainly

explanation.surface: An emphatic statement that this phrase means praising someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds the answer: CR for credit plus YUP for 'certainly!' gives a phrase meaning to praise.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise something loudly or talk it up is to give it credit.

clue.text: Husband embracing duchess who's jilted a PM

indicators.note: embracing means holding something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: man as in 'man and wife', a husband

indicators.note: jilting someone means dropping them, so the named letter is removed

parts.note: Camilla, once Duchess of Cornwall

explanation.surface: A husband keeping hold of a duchess who has thrown over a Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who's jilted a' drops the first A, not any A; 'PM' is the whole definition, and Harold Macmillan was a British Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Macmillan was Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 1957 to 1963.

clue.text: One hunted over drugs in East Germany

parts.note: over in the sense of concerning, about: RE

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other here

parts.note: DDR, the German abbreviation for the former German Democratic Republic
E is ecstasy, so two Es are drugs

explanation.surface: A fugitive pursued over a drugs case in the old East Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is not a reversal here but RE, 'concerning'; drugs as a plural gives two Es, ecstasy being E.
explanation.definitionFit: This large deer is a traditional quarry of stag hunts in Britain.

clue.text: Debutante tougher having shaken off sir's clutches?

indicators.note: shaking something off removes it, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: sinewier, more stringy and tough
the letters of sir, spread around the word as if clutching it

explanation.surface: A young debutante breaking free from an older gentleman's grip.
explanation.walkthrough: S, I and R are removed from SINEWIER in order, leaving the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A debutante is a newcomer, which this informal word for a novice also means.

clue.text: One's not entirely distraught with draw, defying odds!

definitions.text: One's not entirely distraught with draw, defying odds!

indicators.note: distraught means upset and in pieces, so the letters are thrown into disorder
defying the odd letters means taking only the even ones, here the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Someone who beat the odds is hardly upset by the result of the draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defying odds' keeps the even letters of DRAW, R and W; 'distraught' rearranges NOT, ENTIRELY and RW. The whole clue describes the winner.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who won a raffle or lottery prize against long odds is unlikely to be upset by the draw.

clue.text: Good health official treated at most one cause of breakdown?

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
stress is a familiar cause of a nervous breakdown

explanation.surface: A health official treated at most one patient for collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges AT MOST into TOASTM. 'Good health' is a toast, so the official is the woman who proposes toasts at a dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the woman who calls the toasts at a formal banquet, saying 'good health'.

clue.text: How to pull plug when broadcast is ill-timed

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the air, so the sound of the phrase counts

parts.note: you pull a plug out of a sink to drain it

explanation.surface: A television broadcast where sound and picture drift apart badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when broadcast' says the phrase for pulling a plug out of a basin sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Not synchronised means mistimed, with sound and picture not matching.

clue.text: Sweep forgets a house he's been to many times

indicators.note: forgetting something leaves it out, so the named letter goes

parts.note: a sweepstake is a draw

explanation.surface: A chimney sweep forgets a house he has visited many times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgets a' drops the A from DRAW. The definition reads 'times' as eras: the time-travelling Doctor of television has visited many.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC's Time Lord travels through history, visiting many different eras.

clue.text: With revolver, force one to go to work

parts.note: a turner is something that turns or revolves
to prize open is to force

explanation.surface: A gunman forces someone at pistol point to go to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolver' looks like a gun, but here it is anything that turns. The definition means a prize awarded to a work of art.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's best-known contemporary art award goes to an artist for their work.

clue.text: Professional driver making tracks across America

definitions.meaning: Ernie ..., a South African tournament golfer who drives off the tee

explanation.surface: A truck driver making his way along routes across the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: A pro golfer drives the ball; elevated urban railways in the USA are called els.

clue.text: Farewell inscription's best for preventing tears

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, the gravestone inscription, plus 's
top means best

explanation.surface: A gravestone epitaph is the finest consolation for grief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' suggests weeping at a grave, but means rips in cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripstop is a woven nylon fabric reinforced so small rips do not spread.

clue.text: Actress, loudly cheerful, left all contrary

parts.note: P, piano, is musical notation, here taken as its opposite sense; P is the usual crossword letter for loud direction in music
the opposites of cheerful and left are low and right

explanation.surface: A loud, cheerful actress leaves everyone feeling contrary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all contrary' turns both words into their opposites: cheerful becomes LOW, left becomes RIGHT. Joan Plowright was a British stage and screen actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Joan Plowright was an English actress, wife of Laurence Olivier.

clue.text: Work for Callaghan after leaving Downing Street

definitions.meaning: Jim Callaghan, Prime Minister, became a life peer after leaving office

explanation.surface: Finding employment for a former Prime Minister once he leaves Number Ten.
explanation.walkthrough: Downing Street is the Prime Minister's residence; James Callaghan was made a peer after his premiership.
explanation.definitionFit: Conrad's novel shares its title with what a peer named James might be called.

clue.text: Shark fighters run into side winds

parts.note: the Jets fight the Sharks in West Side Story

indicators.note: into places one piece inside another

parts.note: a side is a team
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Fighters battling a shark are driven into the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shark fighters' is the Jets, the gang opposed to the Sharks in West Side Story; R goes into TEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: These fast high-altitude air currents are winds.

clue.text: Illegal to withhold odds for the field

indicators.note: withholding the odd letters keeps only the even-numbered ones

explanation.surface: A ruling that withholding betting odds on a field is unlawful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odds' suggests betting on a race field, but means the odd letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A lea is an old poetic word for a meadow or grassy field.

clue.text: Well done course for consumption outside

parts.note: a way is a route or course
food 'to go' is a takeaway to eat elsewhere

explanation.surface: Praise for a meal course to be eaten outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well done' suggests cooked steak, but is the exclamation of congratulation.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an exclamation of praise, congratulating someone on success.

clue.text: Stop Helianthus shielding the moon

indicators.note: shielding means keeping something within, so the answer sits inside these words

explanation.surface: A sunflower stops shielding someone from moonlight.
explanation.walkthrough: Helianthus is the sunflower genus; the answer is one of the moons of Uranus.
explanation.definitionFit: This small satellite of Uranus is named after a character in Hamlet.

clue.text: Marker found in spotted round counters

indicators.note: round signals turning back, so the whole assembled string is read backwards
in places one piece inside another

parts.note: spotted means seen
a tag is a label or marker

explanation.surface: A felt-tip pen found among spotted round counters in a board game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns the whole assembly backwards, not just one piece; 'counters' is a verb, not game pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate is to cancel out or neutralise, which is what a counter does.

clue.text: Ring used to bring dog from Park by ear

indicators.note: by ear means judged by listening, so the sound of a name counts

parts.note: Gromit, the dog created by animator Nick Park

explanation.surface: A ring used to bring a dog back from the park by its ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Park' looks like a recreation ground, but is Nick Park, creator of Wallace and Gromit.
explanation.definitionFit: A grommet is a metal or rubber eyelet ring lining a hole.

clue.text: Lump when frozen has no mass

indicators.note: having no letter means it is removed

parts.note: frozen fingers are numb
M is the symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A lump of frozen material with no mass.
explanation.definitionFit: A nub is a small knob or lump.

clue.text: One makes champ resentful, losing one time

indicators.note: losing something means dropping it, so the letter goes

parts.note: bitter means resentful
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone causes a champion to become resentful after one defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'champ' reads as a champion, but here is a verb: to chew noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: To champ is to chew or bite, so someone who champs bites.

clue.text: Booked trainee for spells

parts.note: a boy wizard who learns magic at school in a series of books

explanation.surface: A recruit hired for short stints of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Booked' means appearing in books, and 'spells' are magic, not periods of time.
explanation.definitionFit: J K Rowling's hero is a schoolboy wizard studying magic throughout her novels.

clue.text: Old pop duo finally play a live collection

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word is taken

parts.note: a zoo is a collection of live animals

explanation.surface: A retired pop duo finally performs at a live concert compilation.
explanation.walkthrough: Yazoo was a 1980s British synth-pop duo of Alison Moyet and Vince Clarke.
explanation.definitionFit: Yazoo was an English synth-pop duo active in the early 1980s.

clue.text: Tout's old price falling short

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: falling short means one letter short at the end

parts.note: a toll is a charge or price

explanation.surface: A ticket tout's old asking price falls short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tout' looks like a ticket seller, but is the verb meaning to praise or promote.
explanation.definitionFit: To tout something is to promote and praise it.

clue.text: Problems getting home when they're hiking late?

definitions.text: Problems getting home when they're hiking late?

parts.words: Problems getting home when they're hiking late?
parts.note: property sellers who raise the price at the last minute make it hard for buyers to secure a house

explanation.surface: Walkers out late on the hills struggle to find their way home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiking' is raising a price, not walking; 'getting home' is buying a house. In Britain a seller who accepts a higher late offer is said to gazump the buyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sellers who accept a late higher bid cause problems for buyers trying to buy a house.

clue.text: Delay switch to metrication by English

indicators.note: switching means changing over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Britain's slow switch to metric measures, led by the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch to' rearranges METRICATION; E for English follows.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the lag between a stimulus and a person's response to it.
